candidates.approach: Fit a crossing occurrence/hazard model using complete site-time exposure and existing identity labels. Separately study crossing-method classification and transfer uncertainty. No photograph does not mean no crossing without verified camera operation and detection effort.
data: Primary lead

[Udawalawe fence-crossing study](https://doi.org/10.1111/acv.12982). The public supplement lists figures and a per-individual method summary; a complete licensed timestamped event/effort dataset was not located.
Required fields

Camera/site, timestamp, operating effort, crossing/non-crossing exposure, individual label, direction and barrier condition. Positive crossing events alone cannot estimate unconditional site-night crossing probability.
Existing annotations only
Use author-supplied identities and condition/method labels if legally obtained. No new installations, wildlife observations, voltage experiments or expert relabelling.
Bounded core / fallback

One park boundary. Conditional crossing-method analysis among recorded events is a possible reduced study, but changes the question and cannot validate a hazard forecast. Foreign data do not validate Sri Lankan fence behaviour.
Resources, estimated
CPU survival/mixed-effects/boosting, 16 GB RAM and 5–15 GB working storage; optional cached photo features. Corpus size and runtime unmeasured.
Prototype
Historical site-time probabilities and uncertainty with anonymised individuals; no operational fence control.
team: A: condition-aware forecast
Does barrier state improve time/site baselines? H: State features improve effort-adjusted future forecasts.
Train a time-varying occurrence/hazard model.
Static barrier/site/time models; remove state features.
Out-of-time predictive loss across all monitored exposure.
B: individual strategy
Can predictions transfer beyond habitual crossers? H: Partial pooling improves sparse/new-individual predictions.
Train hierarchical history or existing crossing-method models.
Pooled model and individual-frequency lookup; remove history.
Held-out-individual predictions; method accuracy conditional on crossing.
C: reliability under change
Can uncertainty identify unsupported conditions? H: Shift-aware calibration improves reliability versus pooled fitting.
Fit conditional calibration/abstention on a fixed baseline.
Global calibration and rarity score; remove shift features.
Brier/coverage and reliability by site/state, independent of A/B.
evaluation: Primary metric
Brier score or survival log-loss at a predefined site-night horizon, conditional on monitoring. False alerts per monitored night require suitable non-crossing exposure.
Split
Forward blocks and leave-individual/site-out sensitivity; keep repeated frames of a crossing together. Few locations limit national inference.
Baselines
Site/time frequency, logistic mixed-effects/survival model and gradient boosting; identical state/history availability for comparisons.
Ablations
Barrier state, individual history and calibration separately; identity-free comparison for unfamiliar animals.
Uncertainty and errors
Cluster bootstrap by individual/site and temporal blocks; analyse repeat crossers, unknown identities, gate/wire methods and state changes. Report wide intervals for few independent groups.
Useful result without winning
Show that site rates and habitual individuals explain most gains, or that crossing-only records cannot support calibrated hazard prediction.
Interpretation limit
Crossing prediction does not establish fence effectiveness, safe voltage or a causal reduction in conflict.

candidates.title: Detecting elephant calls with reliable false-alarm rates in unfamiliar soundscapes
candidates.area: Audio ML / Sri Lankan elephant-call event detection
candidates.core_gap: Move from selected call clips to leakage-safe continuous-audio reliability
candidates.problem: A sound classifier can score highly on selected clips yet fail on new recordings. Monitoring requires useful event recall, detection latency and false alarms over long recordings, rather than balanced-clip accuracy alone.
candidates.potential_stakeholders: Bioacoustic researchers and offline monitoring-tool developers; no field warning network is proposed.
candidates.gap: Test nuisance-resistant causal detection with recording/day/site holdouts and authentic negative exposure. A detected call is not a measurement of elephant location, movement direction or impending conflict.
candidates.documented: Living with elephants already demonstrates Sri Lanka–Malaysia transfer loss. Learning to rumble already detects/endpoints calls and discusses contextual noise. The remaining reliability design is inferred; elephant-call classification and cross-country transfer are established.
candidates.question: Can nuisance-resistant and latency-bounded learning retain call recall at a fixed false-alarm rate on held-out Sri Lankan recordings without recorder/background shortcuts?
candidates.hypothesis: Recording-aware training and causal context improve event recall at fixed false alarms/hour. Rival explanation: recorder identity, call-enriched sampling or future context inflate results.

candidates.approach: Use log-mel/CNN or cached pretrained audio features with an event head. Study nuisance invariance, causal context and source-validation calibration offline. No new sensors or raw-waveform foundation-model training.
data: Sri Lankan corpus lead

[LDC Asian Elephant Vocalizations](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2010S05): 57.5 hours, 31.25 annotated, Udawalawe 2006–2007. A user agreement and login-dependent fee/access route apply; free university access is unconfirmed.
Negative-exposure limitation

LDC describes recordings largely initiated around calls during daytime park observations. This is not a demonstrated unattended nighttime village sample; no-call spans may not support operational false alarms/hour.
Other sources / code

[Living with elephants](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2025.111272) offers data on request. [AERD author code/weights](https://github.com/CMGeldenhuys/AERD_inference) are public under GPL-3.0. Public weights do not grant audio access or guarantee a clean recording holdout.
Bounded core / fallback

With licensed audio, begin with recording-held-out call detection. If authentic negative exposure is absent, report archived-recording performance and drop field alert-rate claims. Foreign audio can test methods but cannot validate Sri Lankan performance.
Resources, estimated
CPU feature caching; optional 8–12 GB GPU, 16 GB RAM and 20–60 GB storage depending on licensed format/subset. Actual download size, VRAM and runtime unmeasured.
Prototype
Offline waveform/spectrogram with events, latency and confidence; no live wildlife-location publishing or community alerts.
team: A: nuisance resistance
Can training avoid recorder/background shortcuts? H: Recording-aware training improves unseen-recording detection.
Train nuisance-resistant compact embeddings/losses.
Feature logistic regression and compact CNN; remove nuisance objective.
Event recall on unfamiliar recordings.
B: causal context
How much future audio is required? H: Causal context retains useful recall with bounded look-ahead.
Train causal versus bidirectional temporal heads.
Framewise and AST/AERD-style context; remove future frames.
Recall–latency trade-off at matched feature/model budget.
C: calibrated events
Can thresholds transfer without test-recorder tuning? H: Source-group calibration stabilises event reliability.
Fit confidence calibration and event thresholds on source validation only.
Global threshold/temperature scaling; remove grouping.
Calibration and eligible false alarms/hour, or archived-recording error if negative exposure is unsuitable.
evaluation: Primary metric
Event recall at a predefined false-alarm budget/hour only with representative continuous negatives; otherwise event PR-AUC/Brier with an archived-sample interpretation.
Split
Complete sessions/days and recorder/sites where possible; keep overlapping windows and channels together. Remove spoken field-note channels and audit sample rates.
Baselines and code

Band-energy/feature logistic regression, compact CNN/CRNN and [AERD/AST](https://github.com/CMGeldenhuys/AERD_inference). Released LDC-trained weights may contain held-out sessions; use generic audio initialisation and retraining for clean new splits.
Ablations
Nuisance objective, causal context and calibration separately; match negative sampling, event-merging rule and look-ahead. Synthetic mixtures are not sole evidence of real soundscape transfer.
Uncertainty and errors
Session/day block bootstrap and small-head seeds. Analyse low-SNR/overlapping calls, nuisance sources where labelled and recorder changes. Unannotated spans are not automatically negatives.
Useful result without winning
Show that recording leakage or future context explains a gain, or that the corpus cannot estimate unattended-warning false alarms.
Interpretation limit
Silent elephants remain undetectable acoustically. Calls do not establish migration, elephant-presence sensitivity, distance, imminent conflict or reduced harm.
